newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: PROTECTION FOR CHILDREN OF CONVICTED KILLER
New South Wales Attorney General, Jeff Shaw, says all appropriate steps are being taken to ensure the safety of the children of convicted killer, Gregory Kable.
Kable was successful in the High Court yesterday in challenging the validity of legislation which kept him in jail six months after his four-year term for manslaughter ended.
The legislation was introduced because of concern about threatening letters he wrote to various people, including relatives caring for his children, vowing he would get access to the children.
NATIONAL PARK LEVY CRITICISED
Tour operators say the Queensland Government's move to impose a national park fee and increase the Great Barrier Reef levy will put tourists off visiting the region.
Mike Burgess, from Quicksilver Connections, says there's already concern the region can't compete against cheaper overseas holiday destinations.
Mr Burgess says large wholesale travel companies are already saying Australia is very expensive compared to a lot of other destinations.
FREE PORTRAITS OF THE QUEEN
Portraits of the Queen are to be available free, on request, from Government information bookshops.
Federal Administrative Services Minister, David Jull, announced the move.
The portraits were sold until 1992, when they were withdrawn due to lack of demand by the former Government.
But Mr Jull says a number of people have been asking for the portrait in the past six months.
He says giving the portraits away won't cost much.
Mr Jull says Australians should make as much of their national symbols as they can.
CHURCH QUESTIONS HANSON'S COMPASSION
A Catholic Archbishop has hit out at Federal M-P Pauline Hanson's first speech to Parliament saying her wish to cut foreign aid shows a lack of concern about the "global picture".
Archbishop of Canberra-Goulburn, Francis Carroll, says Ms Hanson's taken too narrow a view of compassion.
Ms Hanson says foreign aid funding would be better invested in the generation of jobs in Australia.
The Archbishop says such comments contradict the truth that we're all part of the human family.
VANSTONE REPEATS JOBS CLAIM
Federal Employment Minister, Amanda Vanstone's repeated her claim that the Coalition will be thrown out of Government at the next election if unemployment doesn't fall.
But Senator Vanstone's added a rider.

She now says the electorate won't judge the Coalition too harshly on unemployment if the Government's measures to bring it down, such as the budget and industrial relations reforms, are blocked in the Senate.
If this were to happen, Senator Vanstone believes the Opposition and Democrats would feel a voter backlash.
FEARS FOR MISSING WOMAN AND BABY ALLAYED
Police say they're satisfied a 25-year-old woman and her five-month-old son are safe, despite their disappearance earlier this week.
An appeal was made for the Tweed Heads woman to come forward, when it was feared she could be suffering from post-natal depression and her baby had a breathing complaint, which required oxygen.
Police say Monica Nothdurft contacted family members and a television journalist last night, saying both she and her baby are well.
However, she told them she didn't want her whereabouts revealed at this stage.
CALL FOR INQUIRY INTO SUPERANNUATION
The Federal Opposition believes it will win enough support to hold an inquiry into superannuation in the wake of the Government's Budget changes.
Labor is supporting the Government's increased tax on superannuation for high income earners, but says it has problems with its administration.
Shadow Finance and Superannuation Minister, Senator Nick Sherry, says there are significant problems with the way the tax will be collected.
PHARMACISTS MAY CHARGE FEE
A conference in Canberra has canvassed the idea of a service fee for pharmacists because they're becoming much more than dispensaries of prescription drugs.
The Pharmaceutical Society of Australia has told the Pharmaceutical Manufacturers Conference that pharmacists are becoming much more involved in their customers' health needs.
Associate Professor Peter Carroll says chemists now offer advice on a range of areas, including lifestyle and diet.
NUDE BEACH CREATES DILEMMA
The Queensland Government's new National Park charge may create a dilemma for some visitors.
The State Opposition has questioned where visitors to a Sunshine Coast nudist beach will pin their passes.
Environment Minister Brian Littleproud told Parliament he hoped Deputy Opposition Leader Jim Elder didn't have a personal interest in the beach.

Mr Littleproud says people wanting to visit the beach would be able to buy a pass - confirming checks would be carried out which led the Opposition to suggest a check might have to involve a bodysearch.
